Rationale: URI's‘Second Grade Option'(UM S8.33.32; SGO hereafter) allows students at the beginning of their URI career toretake courses inwhich they received a C-orbelow.
When they do so, the original grade remains on their transcript but is not used in QPA calculations.The only exception to this rule occurs when determining whether students are eligible to graduate with distinction(≥3.3cumlaude,≥3.5magna cumlaude,≥3.7summa cum laude).The QPA to determine eligibility for this honoris calculated using ALL courses taken at the university, including any repeated using the SGO, rather than the QPA printed on the student's transcript.This results in some students who exercised the S GO being ineligible for honors despite having a suitable QPAon their transcript.

The argument for the current approach is comparing two students with the same QPA, one of whom exercised their rights to a SGOand the other who did not,the latter student is more deserving of graduation with distinction than theformer.Put another way,students wishing to courses attempted at the University dates back to the7o's.There was a concern that by not counting all attempts,academic honors could be awarded on an unequal basis(thosethat utilized the2nd grade option could be given the academic honors as students that did not have any courses that qualified for the2nd grade option).In addition,sincethe2nd grade option is not mandatory,it could disenfranchise students who chose to not exercise the2nd grade option who would have otherwise qualified for academic honors had they chosen to use the2ndgrade option at the start of their undergraduate academic career.

My concern if we were to eliminate calculating distinction without taking into account all course attempts would be that distinction at commencement would become less meaningful." Therewas also concern that changing the current policy might affect students who, although initially dismissed from URI for poor grades, significantly improved their academic performance after being readmitted under the ^conditional read mission’ program (UM $8.25.13 - 8.25.16).
Their poor initial performance makes these students functionally ineligible for honors; changing the policy might increase their chances of earning this distinction.
There are two arguments against the current approach.
First, both the SGO and conditional read mission program provide a measure of forgiveness for mistakes made early in a student's career; the same principle should apply to students’ability to graduate with distinction.
Second, many students logically assume that the transcript-listed QPA determines eligibility - the fact that it does not is confusing and engenders hard feelings in soon-to-be-alumni.

We ask the Faculty Senate to consider eliminating the sentence in s8.22.40‘Distinction' that specifies the QPA for graduating with distinction is calculated using all courses attempted at URI.
Its deletion would mean that student eligibility for graduating cum/ magna/summa laude would by default be determined using the transcript-listed QPA.Thiswould eliminate student confusion over their eligibility and ensure that the forgiveness embodied in the SGOand conditional read mission policies applies throughout a student's time at the university.
